title: Forward QA Agents — Field Guide
eyebrow: Plates 44 and 45 of the field guide
footer: Forward QA Agents · two agents an organisation can drop into its own environment · the [process page](process.html) explains the engagement they belong to.
heroH1: Two agents that land in a stranger's environment and leave working test infrastructure behind.
heroLead: Plate 44 points a real browser at a running web app, records what is broken, and provisions a complete Playwright + Playwright MCP project with page objects, a smoke suite and CI. Plate 45 reads whatever legacy test estate already exists — Selenium in Java, Python, C# or JavaScript, Cucumber, Postman, markdown test plans — and rebuilds it as one standardised Playwright architecture with a migration report that lists every line it could not convert. Both run to completion with no model at all; a local open-weight model only polishes text.
primerP: Each agent is one folder under `src/agents/`, one CLI, a handful of REST routes and a `node:test` suite. Every deliverable exists with `LLM_PROVIDER=none`: the crawl, the findings, the generated project, the report. Both persist to the same SQLite database (`engagements`, `runs`, `findings`, `artifacts`) through Node's built-in `node:sqlite`, so every number in a report can be traced to a run id and every generated file to an artifact row. The only model the adapter will talk to is one you run yourself; public endpoints are rejected.
